title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement a new generation of gender-responsive national employment policies, including for youth

description.narrative: In 2020, the Government of Ethiopia through the Jobs Creation Commission (JCC) developed and adopted the National Plan of Action for Jobs Creation (NAPJC) (2020-2025), which contains a youth employment strategy with a focus on establishing job centres as a key strategy on job creation and employment promotions. The rapid impact assessment of the COVID 19 on the jobs and employment situation in the formal and informal economy carried out by the JCC in April 2020, has informed JCC's and Planning commission early response policy. The ILO provided support in terms of commissioning assessments and studies by engaging international and national consultants and building the capacity of JCC and other pertinent partners.

description.narrative:
In 2020, the labour-intensive approach was adopted by the Somali Regional Roads and Transport Bureau (SRRTB) in the implementation of roads maintenance in Jigjiga, and their officials provided on-site supervision and monitoring to contractors using ILO guidelines. The joint refugee camp site assessment on rehabilitation of WASH infrastructures with Agency for Refugees Response Authority (ARRA) provided the agency tools and methodology to carry out similar assessments in the future. With support from The Netherlands, the ILO completed a rapid socio-economic assessment in refugee communities of Somali and Tigray regions focusing on the market around refugee and host workers, with a focus on employment creation as a contributor to social integration. The assessment can be accessed via https://www.ilo.org/global/programmes-and-projects/prospects/WCMS_757830
A localized rapid assessment on the impact of COVID-19 on the refugee and IDP labour market economies in Somali and Tigray regions has been completed (Jun - Aug 2020). The assessment can be accessed via https://www.ilo.org/global/programmes-and-projects/prospects/countries/ethiopia/WCMS_779298/lang--en/index.htm
In July 2020, the ILO completed an inventory and road condition survey to selected road links in Jigjiga and Kebribeyah with a view to create inclusive decent jobs and other economic opportunities using the labour-based approaches. This was coupled with an infrastructural survey to assess possible mitigation measures of the impact of COVID-19 outbreak in the refugee camp of Kebribeyah, and align with the Ethiopian Refugee Preparedness and Response Plan (ERPRP). The assessments were made with ARRA technical staff and identified the need to rehabilitate WASH facilities and the health centre that will accommodate refugees with suspected infection for temporary quarantine and treatment, which were at the time using on-camp school facilities. Joint ILO/ARRA assessment also built the capacity of ARRA in carrying out such exercises in the future.
From 10 – 14 August 2020, the ILO facilitated a training in labour-based technologies in collaboration with the Jigjiga Polytechnic College on roads construction and maintenance for local public and private contractors. The course provided participants with theoretical and practical knowledge on rural/urban infrastructure maintenance of roads.

description.narrative:
The Ethiopian Jobs Creation Commission (JCC) and other authorities made a profound reform of the public employment services environment in Ethiopia. To this effect, in 2020, a "National vision of PES for Ethiopia" was developed in partnership with the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA) and JCC and it is in line with the National Action Plan for Jobs Creation (NAPJC).
In addition to the PES Roadmap, PES service delivery protocols were developed. An assessment of PES service delivery with a focus on the Amhara ES was completed and guidelines for strengthening service offer and delivery were adopted.
Capacity of the JCC in employment services has been developed through hands-on technical assistance of an international expert and ILO experts. A Rural job centre strategy is being developed. The ILO, with support from the Government of Germany, has facilitated negotiations between JCC and MoLSA, and other stakeholders, and provided expert guidance. South-South RBTC funding has been secured to also support this process. This allowed the deployment of an International PES expert to work with the JCC from January to July 2021.
The ILO provided step by step support to the JCC in the development of the roadmap, assessment and development of guidelines, service protocols and service offer at different levels.

Output A.1. More accurate and sustainable statistics on decent work using the latest statistical standards

description.narrative:
The Ethiopian Jobs Creation Commission (JCC) conducted a rapid impact assessment of the COVID 19 on the jobs and employment situation in the formal and informal economy in April 2020. This has informed JCC and Planning commission early response policy.
The ILO initiated a series of Rapid labour force surveys of COVID19 Impact (via phone), to track key labour market indicators throughout the current crisis, and enquire about COVID19 specifics (remote work, etc). The first wave was conducted in August and the second wave in December 2020. The third wave is carried out in July 2021. The ILO provided support in terms of commissioning assessments and studies by engaging international and national consultants and building the capacity of JCC and other pertinent partners.
The ILO conducted a Rapid Skills Assessment (RSA) of the Agro-processing sector during the COVID-19 pandemic', Ethiopia with the objective to identify the skill and labour deficiencies, shortages and surpluses resulting from the impact of the COVID 19 pandemic and to recommend effective reskilling and upskilling measures in the Agro-processing sector. The findings of the assessment used to inform ProAgro- promotion of Decent work in Agribusiness project.
In light of the findings of the Rapid Skills Assessment, the ILO organized the first consultation workshop on establishing a Sector Skills Council (SSC) on Agro Processing in May 2021 in Addis Ababa. The objective of the consultation was to bring together relevant stakeholders and tripartite constituents working in the area of skills development mainly in Agro-processing together and establish a coordination mechanism in the sector to ensure better skills trainings and labour management, which would result in enhancement of productivity.
The diagnostic study found the need to support Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) and the Regional Investment Bureaus (RIB) in the project's target areas – Amhara and Sidama on targeting investors, negotiating incentive offerings, facilitating company project set-up and supporting the retention/expansion of existing investors.
